review_notes: I read the whole file and the related definitions: the `MorphismProperty.Comma` and `Arrow` simp lemmas, `TopCat.Homotopy` (`h`, `h_hom_apply`), and the downstream use in `EilenbergSteenrod.lean`. I found no credible cycles or unwanted expansion. `symm_symm` and the `@[simps]` lemmas look fine. The `Hom.fst`/`Hom.snd`/`map` abbrevs are covered by the existing `comp_hom` and `id_hom` rules. The `Hom.w_apply` and `Homotopy.w_apply` orientations are opposite to `w_apply'`, but they appear confluent via `apply_zero`. The one finding is that `Homotopy.w_apply` is a likely dead or competing local simp rule, and it is hedged because I could not run Lean or see the generated statement. I did not report `w_apply'` as a missing global simp lemma, because keeping these rules local looks like a deliberate choice.

findings.declaration: attribute [local simp] Homotopy.w Homotopy.w_apply (together with w_apply')
findings.problem: The auto-generated `Homotopy.w_apply` is added to the local simp set, but it is probably not usable as a simp rule. By elementwise generation its LHS has the shape `(X.map ▷ _ ≫ fst.h) p`. In the simp set, `TopCat.comp_apply` and `TopCat.Homotopy.h_hom_apply` rewrite exactly that shape (`F.h p = F (I.homeomorph p.2, p.1)`), so `w_apply` is likely shadowed or competing with them. The next lemma, `w_apply'`, shows that it can't be used directly. Its proof has to instantiate `w_apply H (x, I.homeomorph.symm t)` by hand and then call `cat_disch` to reach the normal form `H.fst (t, X.map x) = Y.map (H.snd (t, x))`. So the useful canonical simp rule is `w_apply'`, and `Homotopy.w_apply` is a redundant or ineffective entry in a list that already contains `Homotopy.w` and `w_apply'`. This is hedged, since I could not run Lean or inspect the generated statement.
findings.proposed_change: Drop `Homotopy.w_apply` from the `attribute [local simp]` line, leaving `attribute [local simp] Homotopy.w`. Keep `w_apply'` as the one pointwise simp rule. If that is not enough for the later proofs, use `simp only [w_apply']` where needed. Also give `w_apply'` a docstring or a name that marks it as the simp-normal pointwise form of `Homotopy.w`.
findings.benefit: The simp set has a single pointwise rule for the commuting square, in the `h_hom_apply` normal form. This avoids two overlapping rules for one fact, one of which may never fire. It also makes it clear to readers which lemma `cat_disch` and `simp` actually rely on.

evidence.excerpt: theorem h_hom_apply (p : ↑(X ⊗ I)) : F.h p = F (I.homeomorph p.2, p.1) := rfl
